Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Microwave links
(b) TV and air-conditioner remotes
(c) Thermal-imaging cameras
(d) Infrared heaters and physiotherapy

List-II
(i) Heating
(ii) Night vision
(iii) Point-to-point communication
(iv) Remote control
mcqs.explanation: Microwave links provide point-to-point communication. Infrared radiation is used in TV/AC remotes, thermal-imaging cameras for night vision, and infrared heaters and physiotherapy for heating.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Infrared radiation is used in weather forecasting for cloud and temperature mapping.
Statement B: Motion sensors and night cameras use infrared radiation for security.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Infrared radiation is used for cloud and temperature mapping in weather forecasting and for security applications involving motion sensors and night cameras.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding infrared radiation is correct?
options: Infrared radiation is used only in display screens
Infrared radiation is not used in communication applications
Infrared radiation is used only for weather forecasting
Some infrared wavelengths are used in fibre optics
mcqs.explanation: Some infrared wavelengths are used in fibre optics.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Human vision
(b) Cameras and smartphones
(c) Optical fibres
(d) Lasers

List-II
(i) Seeing the world
(ii) Photography
(iii) Use of some visible wavelengths
(iv) Pointers, surgery and industry
mcqs.explanation: Human vision uses visible light to see the world; cameras and smartphones use it for photography; some visible wavelengths are used in optical fibres; and lasers are used for pointers, surgery and industry.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are applications of visible light?

1. LEDs and bulbs for illumination
2. Visible-light spectroscopy for analysis of materials
3. Monitors and televisions in display screens
mcqs.explanation: All three are applications of visible light: LEDs and bulbs provide illumination, spectroscopy analyses materials, and monitors and televisions use visible light in display screens.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Ultraviolet lamps sterilize by killing bacteria and viruses.
II. UV water filters are used for water purification.
III. Ultraviolet markers on currency and documents help detect forgery.
IV. Vitamin D is synthesized by ultraviolet radiation in human skin.
V. Ultraviolet fluorescence is used for security features and forensic science.
options: I, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: Each of the five statements is correct: ultraviolet radiation is used in sterilization, water purification, forgery detection, Vitamin D synthesis and fluorescence-based security or forensic applications.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Ultraviolet astronomy studies hot stars.
Reason (R): Ultraviolet radiation can cause sunburn and skin cancer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Ultraviolet astronomy studies hot stars, while sunburn and skin cancer are harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation; the latter does not explain the astronomical application.

mcqs.question: Photolithography uses which radiation in semiconductor manufacturing?
mcqs.explanation: Photolithography uses ultraviolet radiation in semiconductor manufacturing.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) X-ray radiographs
(b) CT scans
(c) X-rays in airport security

List-II
(i) Detailed body imaging
(ii) Baggage scanning
(iii) Imaging bones and the chest
mcqs.explanation: X-ray radiographs image bones and the chest, CT scans provide detailed body imaging, and X-rays are used for baggage scanning at airports and in security.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) X-ray crystallography
(b) Industrial X-ray inspection
(c) X-ray astronomy
(d) X-ray cancer treatment

List-II
(i) Study of hot gases and black holes
(ii) Determining the structure of crystals and DNA
(iii) Detecting cracks in metals
(iv) Radiation therapy using high-energy X-rays
mcqs.explanation: X-ray crystallography determines the structure of crystals and DNA; industrial X-rays detect cracks in metals; X-ray astronomy studies hot gases and black holes; and high-energy X-rays are used in cancer radiation therapy.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Gamma-ray radiotherapy kills cancer cells.
II. Gamma rays sterilize medical instruments and food.
III. PET scans and gamma cameras use gamma rays for diagnostic imaging.
IV. Gamma rays are used for thickness gauging and weld inspection in industry.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct applications of gamma rays: cancer treatment, sterilization, diagnostic imaging, and industrial thickness gauging or weld inspection.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Gamma-ray astronomy studies gamma-ray bursts and neutron stars.
II. Nuclear medicine uses radioactive tracers involving gamma rays.
III. Gamma rays are used for detecting nuclear materials in security.
mcqs.explanation: Gamma-ray astronomy studies gamma-ray bursts and neutron stars. Gamma rays are also involved in radioactive tracers used in nuclear medicine and in detecting nuclear materials for security.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength among the listed electromagnetic radiations.
Reason (R): Radio waves have the longest wavelength among the listed electromagnetic radiations.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: gamma rays have wavelengths less than 0.01 nm, while radio waves have wavelengths greater than 1 m. The wavelength of radio waves does not explain why gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Ultraviolet radiation is used for sterilization, vitamin D production, and treating skin diseases.
Statement B: Visible light is used in laser surgery, endoscopy, and illumination.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Ultraviolet radiation has the listed sterilization, vitamin D, and skin-disease applications. Visible light is used in laser surgery, endoscopy, and illumination.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Radio waves in MRI
(b) Infrared radiation
(c) Visible light

List-II
(i) Experimental Li-Fi and some optical fibres
(ii) Radio-frequency pulses
(iii) Remote controls and short-range data communication
mcqs.explanation: MRI uses radio-frequency pulses. Infrared radiation is used in remote controls and short-range data communication, while visible light is used in experimental Li-Fi and some optical fibres.

mcqs.question: Visible and infrared lasers are used for which of the following purposes?
options: Crystallography, CT scans, and baggage scanning
PET scans, gamma cameras, and nuclear medicine
Range finding, targeting, and directed energy
Cloud mapping, temperature mapping, and weather forecasting
mcqs.explanation: Visible and infrared lasers are used for range finding, targeting, and directed energy.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Radio telescopes
(b) Microwaves
(c) Optical telescopes
(d) Ultraviolet astronomy

List-II
(i) Study of hot young stars and the interstellar medium
(ii) Study of stars, galaxies, and planets
(iii) Study of pulsars and the cosmic microwave background
(iv) Study of the Cosmic Microwave Background
mcqs.explanation: Radio telescopes study pulsars and the cosmic microwave background; microwaves are used for Cosmic Microwave Background studies; optical telescopes study stars, galaxies and planets; and ultraviolet astronomy studies hot young stars and the interstellar medium.

mcqs.question: X-ray astronomy studies which of the following?
options: Black holes, neutron stars, and hot gas in clusters
Cool stars, interstellar dust, and exoplanets
mcqs.explanation: X-ray astronomy studies black holes, neutron stars, and hot gas in clusters.

mcqs.question: Which aspect of light explains the photoelectric effect and the Compton effect?
mcqs.explanation: According to the notes, the particle nature of light explains the photoelectric effect and the Compton effect.

mcqs.question: Which medium partially allows light to pass through it?
mcqs.explanation: A translucent medium, such as frosted glass or butter paper, partially allows light to pass through.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
The normal is parallel to the surface at the point of incidence.
The normal is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.
The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is that the normal is stated to be parallel to the surface. According to the notes, it is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.

mcqs.question: A rough surface that produces no clear image exhibits which type of reflection?
mcqs.explanation: Irregular or diffused reflection occurs on rough surfaces and does not produce a clear image.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.
Reason (R): Under these conditions, the entire light is reflected back into the denser medium.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes specify both conditions for total internal reflection and state that the entire light is reflected back into the denser medium.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Plane mirror
(b) Concave mirror
(c) Convex mirror
(d) Convex mirror in vehicles

List-II
(i) Rear-view mirror
(ii) Shaving mirror
(iii) Periscope
(iv) Security mirror
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are plane mirror–periscope, concave mirror–shaving mirror, convex mirror–security mirror and convex mirror in vehicles–rear-view mirror.

mcqs.question: What is the magnification produced by a plane mirror?
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that the magnification of a plane mirror is m = +1.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about mirrors is incorrect?
options: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.
A plane mirror forms a virtual and erect image of the same size.
A concave mirror forms a real and inverted image when the object is beyond C.
A concave mirror forms a virtual and inverted image when the object is within F.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is 'inverted'. When the object is within F of a concave mirror, the image is virtual and erect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: During refraction, the frequency of light remains the same while its wavelength changes.
Statement B: Refraction is caused only by a change in the intensity of light.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that frequency remains the same and wavelength changes during refraction. They identify change in speed and optical density difference, not intensity, as causes.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Lenses
(b) Prisms
(c) Optical fibres
(d) Spectacles

List-II
(i) Correction of eye defects
(ii) Signal transmission
(iii) Converging or diverging light
(iv) Deviation and dispersion
mcqs.explanation: Lenses converge or diverge light, prisms produce deviation and dispersion, optical fibres transmit signals, and spectacles correct eye defects.

mcqs.question: In an optical fibre, which part has the higher refractive index?
mcqs.explanation: An optical fibre consists of a core with higher refractive index and cladding with lower refractive index.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Optical fibres are useful for communication because they have low loss and high bandwidth.
Reason (R): Light remains inside the optical-fibre core through total internal reflection.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that optical fibres use total internal reflection and have the advantages of low loss and high bandwidth.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. An optical fibre uses total internal reflection for communication and endoscopy.
II. A diamond’s sparkle is associated with multiple total internal reflections.
III. A mirage is caused by regular reflection from a plane mirror.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are supported by the notes. A mirage is associated with atmospheric total internal reflection, not regular reflection from a plane mirror.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Endoscope
(b) Mirage
(c) Diamond
(d) Porro prism

List-II
(i) Multiple total internal reflections
(ii) Image inversion without loss
(iii) Medical viewing using optical fibres
(iv) TIR due to atmospheric layers
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are endoscope–medical viewing using optical fibres, mirage–atmospheric TIR, diamond–multiple TIR and Porro prism–image inversion without loss.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about lenses is incorrect?
options: A convex lens is thicker at the centre.
A concave lens is thicker at the edges.
A concave lens is a converging lens.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the description of a concave lens as converging. A concave lens is a diverging lens.

mcqs.question: What is the unit of the power of a lens?
mcqs.explanation: The power of a lens is measured in dioptres (D).

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A convex lens forms a virtual, erect and magnified image when the object is placed within F.
Reason (R): In this position, the convex lens acts as a magnifying glass.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that a convex lens produces a virtual, erect and magnified image within F, which is the principle of a magnifying glass.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Cornea
(b) Iris
(c) Retina
(d) Optic nerve

List-II
(i) Carries signals to the brain
(ii) Controls pupil size
(iii) Main refraction
(iv) Screen where image is formed
mcqs.explanation: The cornea performs the main refraction, the iris controls pupil size, the retina forms the image, and the optic nerve carries signals to the brain.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Myopia causes distant objects to appear blurred.
II. Hypermetropia causes nearby objects to appear blurred.
III. Presbyopia is associated with age-related loss of accommodation.
IV. Astigmatism is caused by clouding of the eye lens.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. Clouding of the eye lens is cataract; astigmatism is due to irregular curvature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about myopia is incorrect?
options: It is corrected using a concave lens.
The image of a distant object forms in front of the retina.
The corrective lens has positive power.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the sign of corrective power. Myopia is corrected with a concave lens having negative power.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Hypermetropia is corrected using a convex lens.
Statement B: Astigmatism is corrected using a cylindrical lens.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that hypermetropia is corrected with a convex lens and astigmatism with a cylindrical lens.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The normal near point is 25 cm.
2. In myopia, the near point is closer than 25 cm.
3. In hypermetropia, the near point is farther than 25 cm.
4. The normal far point is 25 cm.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The normal far point is infinity, not 25 cm.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following steps in the formation of a primary rainbow in the correct sequence:
A. Sunlight enters a water drop.
B. Dispersion takes place.
C. Total internal reflection occurs at the back of the drop.
D. Light refracts out of the drop.
mcqs.explanation: The notes describe the sequence as sunlight entering the water drop, dispersion, total internal reflection at the back, and refraction out.

mcqs.question: Which colour undergoes maximum deviation in dispersion?
mcqs.explanation: Violet has the highest refractive index and undergoes maximum deviation.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The sky appears blue during the day.
Reason (R): Air molecules and dust particles scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly than longer wavelengths.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Rayleigh scattering causes shorter wavelengths to scatter more, producing the blue appearance of the sky.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction.
II. Planets generally do not twinkle because they appear as discs and have an averaging effect.
III. Advance sunrise and delayed sunset are associated with atmospheric refraction.
IV. A mirage is caused by Rayleigh scattering.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. A mirage is associated with total internal reflection caused by atmospheric layers, not Rayleigh scattering.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Light has a dual nature.
Reason (R): Light behaves as a wave and as a particle called a photon.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Light has dual nature because it exhibits both wave behaviour and particle behaviour, the particle being called a photon.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The wave nature of light explains interference.
II. The wave nature of light explains diffraction.
III. The wave nature of light explains polarisation.
mcqs.explanation: Interference, diffraction and polarisation are all explained by the wave nature of light.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: An electromagnetic wave is transverse.
Statement B: An electromagnetic wave does not require a medium.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: An electromagnetic wave is transverse and can propagate without requiring a medium.

mcqs.question: Light travels at its maximum speed in which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Light travels at its maximum speed in vacuum.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Transparent medium
(b) Translucent medium
(c) Opaque medium
(d) Vacuum

List-II
(i) Glass, water and air
(ii) Frosted glass and butter paper
(iii) Wood, metal and stone
(iv) Light travels freely
mcqs.explanation: Transparent media include glass, water and air; translucent media include frosted glass and butter paper; opaque media include wood, metal and stone. Light travels freely in vacuum.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Regular reflection occurs from a smooth surface.
II. Regular reflection produces a clear image.
III. A mirror produces regular reflection.
IV. A wall produces irregular reflection.
V. Paper produces irregular reflection.
options: I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: Smooth surfaces, including mirrors, produce regular reflection and a clear image. Walls and paper produce irregular reflection.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about a plane mirror:
I. It forms a virtual image.
II. It forms an erect image.
III. It forms an image of the same size as the object.
IV. It laterally inverts the image.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object and laterally inverts the image.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Plane mirror used as a looking glass
(b) Plane mirror used in a kaleidoscope
(c) Concave mirror used in headlights
(d) Concave mirror used in a telescope

List-II
(i) Telescope application
(ii) Looking-glass application
(iii) Headlight application
(iv) Kaleidoscope application
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: plane mirror–looking glass, plane mirror–kaleidoscope, concave mirror–headlights and concave mirror–telescope.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following applications of a concave mirror is correctly stated?
options: It is used in a security mirror to provide large-area coverage.
It is used in a street lamp to diverge light over a larger area.
It is used in a solar cooker or furnace to converge sun rays at the focus.
It is used in a rear-view mirror to provide a wide field of view.
mcqs.explanation: A concave mirror is used in a solar cooker or furnace because it converges sun rays at the focus.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about concave-mirror applications:
I. A shaving or makeup mirror produces a magnified erect image when the object is within F.
II. A headlight reflector produces a parallel beam when the bulb is at the focus.
III. A solar cooker or furnace converges sun rays at the focus.
IV. A torch or searchlight produces a strong parallel beam.
V. A dentist mirror produces a magnified image of teeth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: I, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: All five statements correctly describe the listed applications of concave mirrors.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Convex mirror in a street lamp
(b) Rear-view mirror in a vehicle
(c) Security or shop mirror
(d) Mirror in an ATM or parking area

List-II
(i) Large-area coverage
(ii) Wider view for safety
(iii) Wide field of view
(iv) Street-light application
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are street lamp–convex mirror, rear-view mirror–wide field of view, security or shop mirror–large-area coverage, and ATM or parking mirror–wider view for safety.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A rear-view mirror in a vehicle produces an erect and diminished image.
Statement B: A street-light reflector diverges light over a larger area.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The rear-view mirror produces an erect, diminished image, while a street-light reflector diverges light over a larger area.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A reflecting telescope has a large aperture and no chromatic aberration.
Reason (R): These are listed characteristics of a reflecting telescope.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The assertion is true: a reflecting telescope has a large aperture and no chromatic aberration. The reason restates these characteristics and therefore correctly explains the assertion in this question.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): In a plane mirror, the image distance equals the object distance.
Reason (R): A plane mirror laterally inverts the image by reversing left and right.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true characteristics of a plane mirror. However, left-right reversal does not explain why the image distance equals the object distance.

mcqs.question: Light refracts when it passes between which of the following types of media?
options: Vacuum and an opaque medium only
mcqs.explanation: Refraction occurs when light passes between rarer and denser media.

mcqs.question: Sound is best described as which of the following?
options: A mechanical transverse wave requiring vacuum
An electromagnetic transverse wave that travels through vacuum
A mechanical longitudinal wave requiring a material medium
A stationary wave that cannot travel through liquids
mcqs.explanation: Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave and requires a material medium such as a solid, liquid or gas. It cannot travel through vacuum.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Sound travels through air at approximately 340–343 m/s at 20–25°C.
Sound travels through steel or iron at approximately 5000–6000 m/s.
Sound travels through glass at approximately 340–343 m/s.
Sound travels through water at approximately 1480–1500 m/s.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the speed in glass. Sound travels through glass at approximately 5000–6000 m/s, not 340–343 m/s.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A sound having a higher frequency generally has a higher pitch.
Reason (R): Pitch is the sensation of frequency in the brain.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Frequency determines pitch, and pitch is the brain's sensation of frequency; therefore, the reason explains the assertion.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Amplitude determines the loudness or intensity of sound.
Statement B: Amplitude has no effect on the speed, frequency or pitch of sound.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude determines loudness or intensity. It does not affect the speed, frequency or pitch of sound.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about human hearing:
I. The human audible range is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
II. Infrasonic sound has a frequency above 20 kHz.
III. Human hearing is most sensitive around 2000–4000 Hz.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. Infrasonic sound is below 20 Hz, whereas sound above 20 kHz is ultrasonic.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Guitar
(b) Flute
(c) Tabla
(d) Cymbals

List-II
(i) Vibration of stretched membrane
(ii) Vibration of air column
(iii) Vibration of strings
(iv) Vibration of plates or solids
mcqs.explanation: Guitar uses vibrating strings, flute uses a vibrating air column, tabla uses a stretched membrane, and cymbals use vibrating plates or solids.

mcqs.question: At a speed of 340 m/s in air, what is the wavelength of a 20 Hz sound wave?
mcqs.explanation: For a 20 Hz sound in air at 340 m/s, the wavelength is 17 m. The 20 kHz sound has a wavelength of 1.7 cm.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about amplitude is incorrect?
options: The unit of amplitude is metre.
The energy of sound is proportional to the square of its amplitude.
Amplitude is the distance between two successive compressions.
Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from their mean position.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the definition. The distance between two successive compressions is wavelength, whereas amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The speed of sound increases with an increase in temperature.
Reason (R): The speed of sound increases by approximately 0.61 m/s for every 1°C rise in temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The stated increase of approximately 0.61 m/s per °C directly describes why the speed rises with temperature.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Medical imaging
(b) Industrial testing
(c) SONAR
(d) Cleaning

List-II
(i) Detecting cracks or flaws in metals
(ii) Ultrasonic cleaning of delicate parts or jewellery
(iii) Ultrasound scanning or sonography
(iv) Underwater detection
mcqs.explanation: Medical imaging uses sonography, industrial testing detects cracks or flaws in metals, SONAR performs underwater detection, and ultrasonic cleaning is used for delicate parts or jewellery.

mcqs.question: SONAR is based primarily on which of the following principles?
options: Reflection of ultrasonic waves and measurement of the time interval
Absorption of infrasonic waves by water
mcqs.explanation: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It sends ultrasonic pulses, receives their reflections from an object and measures the time interval.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about infrasound is incorrect?
options: Infrasound can be used for weather monitoring of storms and tornadoes.
Seismic waves can contain infrasonic frequencies.
Elephants and whales use infrasound for communication.
SONAR uses infrasound for underwater detection.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the wave type used by SONAR. SONAR uses ultrasound, not infrasound, for underwater detection.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): When a sound source approaches an observer, the apparent frequency and pitch increase.
Reason (R): The Doppler effect is an apparent change in frequency caused by relative motion between the source and observer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The relative motion in the Doppler effect causes the approaching source to be heard at a higher apparent frequency and pitch.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following descriptions of musical instruments are correct?

I. Guitar produces sound through vibration of strings.
II. Flute produces sound through vibration of an air column.
III. Tabla produces sound through vibration of plates or solids.
IV. Cymbals produce sound through vibration of a stretched membrane.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. Tabla uses a stretched membrane, while cymbals use vibrating plates or solids; therefore, two descriptions are correct.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum distance required for a distinct echo to be heard by the human ear?
mcqs.explanation: The minimum distance for an echo to be heard by the human ear is approximately 17.2 m, based on the persistence of hearing of 0.1 second.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Sound propagates through compressions and rarefactions.
II. The speed of sound in a vacuum is zero.
III. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Sound propagates through compressions and rarefactions. In a vacuum its speed is zero, and sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

mcqs.question: Which of the following represents the general order of the speed of sound in different media?
mcqs.explanation: The general speed order of sound is solid > liquid > gas.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Frequency is the number of vibrations per second.
II. Frequency is the number of compressions per second.
III. The unit of frequency is hertz (Hz).
IV. Frequency determines the pitch of sound.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency represents the number of vibrations or compressions per second, is measured in hertz, and determines the pitch of sound.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): At a fixed speed of sound, a higher frequency corresponds to a smaller wavelength.
Reason (R): In air at 340 m/s, a sound of frequency 20 kHz has a wavelength of 1.7 cm.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 20 kHz example illustrates the wavelength value, but it does not itself explain the general inverse relation between frequency and wavelength.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Low frequency
(b) Male voice
(c) High frequency
(d) Whistle

List-II
(i) Bass or deep sound
(ii) Example of a bass or deep sound
(iii) Shrill sound
(iv) Example of a shrill sound
mcqs.explanation: Low frequency produces a bass or deep sound, with the male voice as an example. High frequency produces a shrill sound, with a whistle as an example.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relation between pitch and frequency?
options: Pitch is directly proportional to frequency
Pitch is determined only by amplitude
Pitch is inversely proportional to frequency
mcqs.explanation: Pitch is directly proportional to frequency.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Pitch is independent of amplitude or loudness.
Statement B: Loudness is directly related to amplitude.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Pitch does not depend on amplitude or loudness, while loudness is directly related to amplitude.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Quality or timbre
(b) Same pitch and loudness
(c) Waveform
(d) Overtones

List-II
(i) Sounds can still be distinguished by their quality
(ii) Characteristic that distinguishes two sounds
(iii) A factor on which timbre depends
(iv) Another factor on which timbre depends
mcqs.explanation: Quality or timbre distinguishes sounds having the same pitch and loudness. It depends on the waveform and the overtones present.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Quality or timbre
(b) Same note on different instruments
(c) More overtones
(d) Periodic waveform

List-II
(i) Produces richer quality
(ii) Shape determines quality
(iii) Depends on harmonics present
(iv) Can sound different on flute, violin and piano
mcqs.explanation: Quality or timbre depends on the harmonics present and is determined by the shape of the periodic waveform. The same note on a flute, violin and piano can sound different, while more overtones produce richer quality.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The speed of sound at 0°C is approximately 331 m/s.
Statement B: The speed of sound at 20°C is approximately 343 m/s.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The speed of sound is approximately 331 m/s at 0°C and approximately 343 m/s at 20°C.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Sound travels fastest through solids.
Reason (R): Solids have high elasticity or bulk modulus, and their molecules are closely packed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Sound travels fastest through solids because their high elasticity or bulk modulus and closely packed molecules favour faster propagation.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Sound travels at an intermediate speed through liquids, which are less elastic than solids.
II. Sound travels slowest through gases because gases have low elasticity.
III. The molecules in gases are far apart.
IV. The general order of the speed of sound is solid > liquid > gas.
V. A train sound is heard better through rails than through air.
options: I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV and V
II, III, IV and V only
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. Sound has intermediate speed in liquids and the slowest speed in gases; the overall order is solid > liquid > gas, and train sounds are heard better through rails than through air.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The audible sound frequency range is 20 kHz.
II. The human hearing limit decreases with age.
III. The decrease in the human hearing limit with age is especially significant for higher frequencies.
mcqs.explanation: The audible sound frequency range extends to 20 kHz. The human hearing limit decreases with age, particularly for higher frequencies.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Echocardiography
(b) Pest control
(c) Welding and drilling
(d) Precision machining

List-II
(i) Driving away insects and rodents
(ii) Imaging the heart
(iii) Industrial application involving precision machining
(iv) Industrial application involving welding and drilling
mcqs.explanation: Ultrasound is used in echocardiography to image the heart, in pest control to drive away insects and rodents, and in industry for welding, drilling and precision machining.
